name: Patricia Lang
life: “I still remember a polishing cloth cut from a party dress.” People around the foot of Harbor Viaduct know Patricia by a small Saturday habit. Patricia pauses where the machinery overhead makes two people stand close enough to hear each other.
voice: I want to polish just the bit her thumb wore bright. Nothing else remembers a hand so precisely.
appearance: Patricia is easy to recognize by a long plait tucked inside the collar and a straight nose and deep-set eyes. Usually dressed in a faded indigo overshirt with one cuff folded back twice, Patricia listens with the head tilted a little to the left when listening.
personality: Patricia is patient with a person learning and fiercely impatient with somebody pretending to know. A half-finished job left where a beginner can see it is an invitation, as far as Patricia is concerned.
agenda: To preserve the bright place where the thumb rested.
family: Grey Lopez is Patricia’s stepsibling. Patricia saves a place. Grey chooses whether to use it. The invitation means something because declining it has never ended the friendship between their households. Asked about *The porch auction*, Grey says, “I always envied their porch. Buying a chair taught me I liked the people who sat on it more.”
connections: Albert Bennett (razor sharpener). They work out where to polish the blade and where to keep the thumbprint bright.

reactions.situation: The widow wants to tell the apprentice who held it first
reactions.response: Patricia makes space for the widow and the apprentice to talk without buyers listening.

reactions.situation: A frightened child is waiting outside a shuttered shop
reactions.response: Patricia lets the child choose whether to stand by the door or sit beside the window while another adult gets help.
